clue.text: Determining age of a metal key found by 007 beside vehicle

indicators.note: beside says the vehicle sits next to the spy in the answer
found by says the a-metal-key string comes next to the spy, after him

explanation.surface: James Bond, parked by his car, discovers a metal key and has its age worked out.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are given in reverse order of the answer: 'beside' and 'found by' put the car first, then Bond, then A, TIN and G.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiocarbon dating is the scientific method of measuring how old organic remains are.

clue.text: Instrument identified by man in Church Army

indicators.note: in says the man's name is placed inside the church-and-army letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An instrument recognised by a man serving in the Church Army, a Christian evangelistic charity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Church Army' reads as one real organisation, but it must be split into two separate abbreviations, church and army.
explanation.definitionFit: A celesta is a keyboard percussion instrument with metal bars, heard in the Sugar Plum Fairy dance.

clue.text: Clamouring for ropes in stormy ocean tracts

parts.note: clamouring means roaring, making a loud noise
ropes are ties, things used for tying

explanation.surface: Sailors loudly demand ropes while crossing rough stretches of sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roaring Forties are the windy latitudes between 40 and 50 degrees south, famous for gales and heavy seas.

clue.text: Surgical procedure overcoming twitching of the eye

indicators.note: in a down clue, overcoming says the first piece sits above, on top of, the second

parts.note: an op is an operation, a surgical procedure
a tic is an involuntary twitching

explanation.surface: An eye operation that cures a twitch of the eyelid.
explanation.definitionFit: Optic is an adjective relating to sight and the eye, as in the optic nerve.

clue.text: Yorkshire fellow originally delivering drinks to crew

indicators.note: originally says take the opening letter of delivering

parts.note: to man a ship is to crew it

explanation.surface: A Yorkshireman who started out bringing beer to a ship's crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crew' is a verb here: to man. The Yorkshire Dales are upland valleys in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A dalesman is a man from the Dales, the valley country of Yorkshire.

clue.text: Part of system protecting casual worker

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A security system that shields a short-term employee.
explanation.definitionFit: A temp is a temporary worker, taken on casually for a short period.

clue.text: Early Christian confusing to a sinner

indicators.note: confusing says the letters of to a sinner are jumbled up

explanation.surface: An early church doctrine baffles a sinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Nestorians followed Nestorius, a fifth-century patriarch whose teaching on Christ's nature was condemned as heresy.

clue.text: Flyer exulted so vocally, welcoming young male castaway

indicators.note: welcoming says the outer string takes the young male inside it

parts.note: a robin is a bird, a flyer

indicators.note: vocally says the words are as heard when spoken

parts.note: crew, the old past tense of crow, means exulted; add so
a son is a young male

explanation.surface: A bird crowed with joy as it welcomed a boy to the island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crew' is the old past tense of 'crow', to exult, as in 'the cock crew'; 'vocally' turns that plus 'so' into the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Defoe's hero is the most famous shipwrecked sailor in fiction, stranded alone on an island.

clue.text: Distribute notes on drama, turning out article for nothing

parts.note: D and E are musical notes

indicators.note: turning out says the article is evicted from the drama word
for says the nothing is put in place of the article

explanation.surface: Spreading musical notes across a play while swapping a word for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: PLAY with A swapped for O gives PLOY.
explanation.definitionFit: To deploy troops or resources is to spread them out where needed, a synonym of distribute.

clue.text: Labour leader takes direction — the bare minimum!

indicators.note: leader says take the opening letter of Labour

explanation.surface: The Labour Party leader heads a direction that delivers almost nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The least is the smallest possible amount, which is what the bare minimum means.

clue.text: Building material this person included in first catalogue

indicators.note: included in says the speaker is put inside the catalogue phrase

parts.note: list one is the first catalogue
this person is the speaker, me

explanation.surface: Someone listed in the opening catalogue of building supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this person' is the setter talking about themselves, giving ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Limestone is a sedimentary rock widely quarried and cut for building blocks.

clue.text: Carrier having legal proceedings connected to diamonds, perhaps

indicators.note: connected to says the two pieces are joined end to end

parts.note: diamonds is one example of a card suit
a case is a lawsuit, legal proceedings

explanation.surface: A courier carries papers for a lawsuit concerning stolen diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'legal proceedings' suggests SUIT, but it is the CASE; the SUIT comes from the cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitcase is a piece of luggage for carrying clothes and belongings.

clue.text: Backslapping woman with little bottle

parts.note: a vial is a small bottle

explanation.surface: A hearty, back-slapping woman holding a small bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: Backslapping describes hearty, effusive friendliness, which is a jolly, good-humoured manner.

clue.text: Like Virgil's works, say, noble and detailed

indicators.note: detailed is read as de-tailed: the word and loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Virgil's poetry, described as lofty and intricately wrought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' is read as de-tailed, docking the D of AND.
explanation.definitionFit: Augustan literature is the golden age of Roman writing under the emperor Augustus, when Virgil wrote.

clue.text: Violently beat son in heretic's garment

indicators.note: violently says the letters of beat son in are thrown about

explanation.surface: A boy is beaten savagely while wearing a heretic's robe.
explanation.definitionFit: The sanbenito was the yellow penitential tunic the Spanish Inquisition made condemned heretics wear.

clue.text: Shame about limits of grass in animal enclosure

indicators.note: about says the shame word goes round the grass letters
limits of says take the outside letters of grass

explanation.surface: It is a pity there is grass round the edges of a farm pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigsty is the fenced pen where pigs are kept.

clue.text: Walk round pub hosting end of international summit

indicators.note: hosting says the result takes in one more letter
round says the walk word is wrapped about the pub
end of says take the last letter of international

explanation.surface: Walking around a pub hosting the end of an international match, near a mountain top.
explanation.walkthrough: Two insertions in turn: the first makes PINNACE, a ship's boat, and 'hosting' then adds the last letter of 'international'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinnacle is a high peak or pointed top, the same idea as a summit.

clue.text: Pulverised earth

definitions.meaning: crushed into powder, as coffee beans are
soil, the surface we stand on

explanation.surface: Earth crushed into powder.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground is the past participle of grind, meaning crushed; as a noun it means the soil or earth.

clue.text: Petulant medic imbibing spirit before close of party

indicators.note: before says the doctor-and-drink piece comes ahead of the next letter
imbibing says the doctor drinks in, takes inside, the spirit

parts.note: a GP is a general practitioner, a doctor

indicators.note: close of says take the last letter of party

explanation.surface: A sulky doctor knocking back rum before the party ends.
explanation.walkthrough: GP is a general practitioner, the British family doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Petulant means sulky and bad-tempered, a close synonym of crabby or irritable.

clue.text: Charming lass's last gains

indicators.note: last says take the final letter of lass's

explanation.surface: A charming girl's final profits.
explanation.definitionFit: Winnings are money gained from a bet or game, so they are gains.

clue.text: Way informer turned up, trapping quiet family member

parts.note: St is short for street, a way

indicators.note: trapping says the informer word holds the quiet letter inside it
in a down clue, turned up says the informer word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a nose is slang for a police informer
p is piano, quiet in music

explanation.surface: An informer, having turned up on the street, holds a silent relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses NOSE to ESON in a down light; 'trapping' places P inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepson is the son of one's spouse, a relative by marriage.

clue.text: Released at one, reversing it in the centre

indicators.note: says only the two central letters, the word it, are turned round

parts.note: at one means united, in agreement

explanation.surface: Someone set free at one o'clock, turning things around at the centre.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle two letters of UNITED are IT; flipping them gives TI.
explanation.definitionFit: Untied means unfastened, set loose from bonds, so freed or released.

clue.text: Sphere of activity of one dipping into a French poem?

indicators.note: dipping into says the one letter goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A poet dabbling in a French poem asks what field he works in.
explanation.definitionFit: Universe can mean a whole sphere or realm of activity or thought, as in her own little universe.

clue.text: Instinctive feelings exist between woman and son

indicators.note: between says the exist word sits in the middle of the other two

explanation.surface: Gut feelings that live between a woman and her son.
explanation.definitionFit: Vibes are informal emotional signals one picks up intuitively from a person or place.

clue.text: Bovine creature young kids raised

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised says the word reads upwards, back to front

explanation.surface: A calf that small children have reared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kids' suggests goats, but means children here.
explanation.definitionFit: A stot is a dialect word for a young bullock or steer, a member of the cattle family.

clue.text: Greek character curiously cites it as over-godly

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: curiously says the letters of cites it are arranged oddly

explanation.surface: A Greek man oddly quotes something as excessively religious.
explanation.definitionFit: Pietistic describes an exaggerated, sanctimonious show of devoutness, overly religious.

clue.text: Fish one consumed as main ingredient

indicators.note: consumed says the fish has swallowed the one letter

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A fish eaten as the centrepiece of a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: The basis of a mixture is its chief component, the foundation of the recipe.

clue.text: Like Tyneside woman uncompromising about article?

indicators.note: about says the woman goes round the article

explanation.surface: A stern Geordie woman lecturing on a newspaper article.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyneside is the Newcastle area in the north-east of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyneside lies in the north-east of England, so it is described by that regional adjective.
